title: Self-Supervised Doppler-Guided RF Odometry
claim: A single self-supervised, sensor-only model recovers ego-motion from raw signals while staying robust to dynamic scenes and poor visibility.
layout: 2 panels split by dashed line; left pipeline plus property strip, right scene illustration
description: The left panel is a rounded blue-bordered card titled 'Self-supervised RF-only odometry'. A simple flow runs left to right. Stacked range-azimuth heatmaps at frames t and t+1 (X_t = [I_t, V_t^dop]) feed a blue box labeled 'RFWalk: Physics-informed self-supervised correspondence learning'. Its output is an ego-motion estimate T_{t→t+1} ∈ SE(2), shown as a faded robot at t and a dark robot at t+1 joined by a dashed arrow. A pink strip along the bottom lists four properties: RF-only, Self-supervised, Dynamic-scene robust and Visibility robust. The right panel is a top-down rendering of an indoor office. A blue trajectory runs from a red start dot to the robot, with moving pedestrians marked by orange arrows and a legend in the corner. A row of range-azimuth heatmaps below shows the RF observations along the path.
caption: Self-supervised RF-only odometry. Left: from consecutive RF frames alone, RFWalk learns cross-frame correspondences without pose labels or auxiliary sensors and recovers the ego-motion Tt→t+1. Right: illustration of RF-only odometry in a dynamic indoor scene with moving pedestrians.
abstract: Radio-frequency (RF) sensing enables robot ego-motion estimation in darkness, smoke, and fog, yet RF odometry remains challenging because multipath and moving reflectors make cross-frame matching highly ambiguous. Existing methods often rely on auxiliary inertial sensors or ground-truth pose supervision. We present RFWalk, a self-supervised, RF-only odometry framework that models dense correspondences across range-azimuth frames as random walks on a space-time graph and learns them from unlabeled sequences through temporal cycle consistency. To rule out correspondences that are cycle-consistent but physically implausible, we introduce a Doppler consistency loss that constrains correspondence-induced motion using radial velocity measured by the RF sensor itself. Ego-motion is then recovered through robust $\mathrm{SE}(2)$ registration that suppresses uncertain correspondences and those arising from independently moving objects. Without pose labels or auxiliary sensors, RFWalk remains competitive with supervised baselines in static scenes and reduces absolute trajectory error by 58% in dynamic scenes with moving pedestrians.
